la:verb:ineo.html:
ĭn-ĕo, īvi and ĭi, ĭtum, īre (iniri only ap. ;
fut. iniet, ), v. a. and n.
To go into, to enter a place (class.).
Lit.
In gen., constr. with acc., or with in and acc.
With acc.: illius domum,: urbem,: Argolicas acies non ignarus ini (i. e. inii),: convivia,: viam, iter,to enter on a journey,.—Pass.: nemus nullis illud initur equis,: (Hispania) prima Romanis inita provinciarum,.—
With in and acc.: in urbem,.—
In partic., to know, in mal. part., : reginam, Drusillam, Anton. ap. : feminae viros ineunt,; so of animals,to pair,; .—Pass.: vacca ab agresti tauro inita,; cf.: sic velut inita arbor fecundo semine fertilior exstat,.—
Trop., to enter upon, begin a business, an enterprise, occupation, office, etc.: magistratum,: consulatum,: imperium,.—Pass.: inito magistratu,: magnum et difficile certamen iniens,; : proelium,; ; ; : pugnas,: bellum,.—Pass.: bellum cum rege Philippo initum est,; : numerum, to go into an enumeration, i. e. to enumerate, give the number: numerus interfectorum haud facile iniri potuit,: numerus inibatur,: rationem, to make an estimate: rationem inire oportet operarum, dierum,; cf.: initā subductāque ratione,: inire rationem also freq. signifies, to calculate, consider, find out, devise, contrive: rogo, ut adjuves ineasque rationem, quemadmodum ea mulier Romam perducatur,: mihi ineunda ratio, et via reperiunda est, qua ad Apronii quaestum possim pervenire,. § 110: ut multa tam gravis depelleretur, a me inita ratio est. : rationem de re,: ad hunc interficiendum talem iniit rationem,: aestimationem,to make an estimate, to estimate, value,: mensuram agrorum,to take the measure of, to measure, survey,: societatem cum aliquo, to enter into or form an association with a person, Planc. ap. ; so of an alliance, : bellum,to take part in,; : pugnas,to begin,: pugnam,; : indutias,to conclude, make,: consilium,to form a plan, : consilia inibat, quemadmodum a Gergovia discederet,formed plans, considered, deliberated,: consilium facinoris contra vitam alicujus,: gratiam, to get into the good graces, obtaĭn the favor of: plures ineuntur gratiae, si, etc.,the favor of many is gained,: gratiam ab aliquo,: apud regem initam gratiam volebant,: summam gratiam a bonis omnibus,: viam, to find out a way to do any thing: ineamus viam aliquam, qua utri utris imperent, decerni possit,: suffragia, i. q. dare,; : inită aestate,in the beginning of,; ; cf.: inită hieme,.—Poet.: somnum,to fall asleep,: ipse ego paulisper pro te tua munera inibo,to undertake,: formam vitae,to enter upon a course of life,: teque adeo decus hoc aevi, te consule (puer), inibit, Pollio,he will enter on this golden age during your consulship, Ladew.; cf. Forbig. ad loc.—
v. n. (= incipere), to make a beginning, to begin: ex ineunte aevo,; so, ineunte vere,: ineunte aestate,: ab ineunte aetate,: ab ineunte adulescentia,; ; cf.

ineptus
,

Plur.: ĭneptĭae, ārum, sillinesses, fooleries, trifles, absurdities (class.): omnium ineptiarum haud scio an ulla sit major, quam, etc.,; ; : paene aniles,: sententiarum,: hujusmodi ineptiis se immiscere, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 2, 3.

to talk or act strangely or absurdly

id.
,
to talk or act absurdly, to trifle, play the fool (poet.): ineptis,; : desinas ineptire,.

la:adj:inermis.html:
ĭn-ermis, e, and in-ermus, a, um (v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 88), adj.
2. in-arma
,
unarmed, without weapons, defenceless.
Form inermis.
Lit.: si spoliatum, inermem recepisset Antonium,: inermibus vim facere (opp. arma. tis),; cf. ; sq.: milites,: manus peditum inermium, Brut. ap. : praedas ex agro inermi ac nudo praesidiis agens,; cf. : frater tendebat inermes infelix palmas,; ; : inermia frustra bracchia tendens,.—
Transf.: legati,without an army,; cf. ; 3, 5: gingiva,toothless,: virus,weak,.—
Trop.: carmen,i. e. that wounds no one, harmless,; cf. : in altera philosophiae parte inermis ac nudus est,unprepared, not well versed,: omnia tractanda putabat inermi justitia,.—
Form inermus: cum paucis inermis (al. inermibus),: magna multitudo sed inermorum, Lepid. ap. : ab inermis pedibus, (in other passages of Sall. the read. is dub.; cf. Kritz, J. 113, 6; Fabri,).

la:noun:inertia.gloss: want of art or skill, unskillfulness, ignorance
senses: want of art or skill, unskillfulness, ignorance
la:noun:inertia.html:
ĭnertĭa, ae, f.
id.
,
want of art or skill, unskilfulness, ignorance.
Lit. (rare but class.): animi (spectantur), quemadmodum affecti sint, virtutibus, vitiis; artibus, inertiis,; . —
Transf., in gen., inactivity, idleness, laziness (very freq.): inertia atque torpedo, Cato ap. : id largiamur inertiae nostrae,: castigare segnitiem hominum atque inertiam,: laboris,aversion to labor,: operis,— In an oxymoron: strenua,; cf. inquieta,.

la:adj:ineluctabilis.html:
ĭn-ēluctābĭlis, e, adj.,
from which one cannot extricate one's self, unavoidable, inevitable (poet. and post-Aug.).
Lit.: caenum,.—
Trop.: tempus,: fatum,;

la:adj:iners.gloss: without skill, unskilled, unskillful, incompetent, crude
senses: without skill, unskilled, unskillful, incompetent, crude
inactive, lazy, idle, indolent, sluggish, inert; worthless; stagnant
quiet, timid, tame, docile, spiritless, cowardly
la:adj:iners.html:
ĭners, ertis (abl. inerti, :
inerte,; ), adj.
2. in-ars
, unskilled in any art or trade, without skill, unskilful (class.): ut perhibetur iners, ars in quo non erit ulla, Lucil. ap. : artes, quibus qui carebant, inertes a majoribus nominabantur,: versus, artless ( = sine arte et gravitate facti), .—In partic., = iners dicendi, arte dicendi carens: homo non inertissimus,. —
In gen., inactive, idle, indolent, sluggish, inert.
Of living beings: linguā factiosi, inertes operā,: silvicolae homines bellique inertes, Naev. ap. : gerro, iners, etc.,: vicissent inprobos boni fortes inertes,: senectus,: homo inertior, ignavior proferri non potest,: pecus,; cf.: fera membris,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: inertissimum et desidiosissimum otium,: inertissima segnitia,: ignavum et iners genus interrogationis,empty, idle,: aquae,stagnant waters,: stomachus,i. e. without digestion,: glaebae,that bear nothing, without cultivation,: terra,motionless, immovable,: horae,leisure hours,: tempus,: Brutus castigator lacrimarum atque inertium querellarum,.— Of food, without flavor, insipid: caro,: blitum iners videtur, ac sine sapore, aut acrimonia ulla,: sal,:

vita, inactive, quiet, . — Poet., causative, rendering idle or inactive: frigus,: somni,. — Hence, adv.: ĭnerter, and sup. inertissime, P.

la:adj:inexpertus.gloss: untried, not having tried, unused, unproven
senses: untried, not having tried, unused, unproven
inexperienced in, unaccustomed to a thing
la:adj:inexpertus.html:
ĭn-expertus, a, um, adj.,
untried (not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Act., that has not madetrial of, unacquainted with, inexperienced in, unaccustomed to a thing: qui lascivia inexperti advenerant,: exercitus bonis inexpertus atque insuetus,: animus ad contumeliam inexpertus,: dulcis inexpertis cultura potentis amici: expertus metuit,.—
Pass., that has not been tried, untried, unproved: legiones civili bello inexpertae,; : fides,: potestas,: carmen,new,: ne quid inexpertum relinquat,; ; : haud tibi inexpertum curvos deprendere mores,

la:adj:inextricabilis.html:
ĭn-extrīcābĭlis, e, adj.
2. in-extrico
,
that cannot be disengaged or disentangled, inextricable (poet. and post-Aug.).
Lit.: error (of the mazes of the labyrinth, from which one could not find his way out),: cortex, that cannot be disengaged or separated. : litus,where one cannot disembark,.—
Trop.: errores,: Stomachi inextricabilia vitia,incurable,: perfectio,inexplicable, indescribable,.—* Adv.: ĭnextrīcābĭlĭter, inextricably: contorta fatorum licia,.

la:adj:inexhaustus.html:
ĭn-exhaustus, a, um, adj.,
unexhausted (poet. and post-Aug.): metalla,: urbes,not plundered,: pubertas,not enfeebled,; (but not in ; v. Madv. ad h. l.).

la:adj:ineffabilis.html:
ĭn-effābĭlis, e, adj.,
unutterable, unpronounceable (Plinian): nomina, § 1: verba,.— Adv.: ĭneffābĭlĭter, unutterably, ineffably (late Lat.): Deus ineffabiliter artifex,.

la:adj:inexpiabilis.html:
ĭn-expĭābĭlis, e, adj.
2. in-expio
,
that cannot be atoned for, inexpiable (class.): religio,: scelus, Auct. Har. Resp. 27.—
Transf., implacable, irreconcilable, obstinate: bellum,; ; : odium Romanorum in Hannibalem, Drak. N. cr.; 2, 17, 2: invidia,.— Adv.: ĭn-expĭābĭlĭter, inexpiably, irremediably: corruptus,.

la:adj:ineruditus.html:
ĭn-ērŭdītus, a, um, adj.,
uninstructed, unlearned, illiterate, ignorant, awkward (class.): non ergo Epicurus ineruditus, sed ii indocti, qui, etc.,: ne quis illud tam ineruditum absurdumque respondeat,: judex,; cf prooem. § 26.— Of abstr. things: voluptates,unrefined, coarse,.—Adv.: ĭnērŭdītē, unlearnedly, ignorantly, awkwardly (post-Aug.): non inerudite ad declamandum ficta materia,.

la:verb:inebrio.gloss: to inebriate someone, make someone drunk, intoxicate
senses: to inebriate someone, make someone drunk, intoxicate
to saturate something with a liquid (e.g. overwatering plants)
la:verb:inebrio.html:
ĭn-ēbrĭo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to make drunk, inebriate (poet. and post-Aug.).
Lit.: palma vescentes inebriat,; ; . —
Transf., of colors, to saturate' amethystum inebriatur Tyrio, .— Of plants: inebriatae radices, i. q. nimis irrigatae,.—
Trop.: aurem,to fill full of talk,.

la:adj:ineptus.html:
ĭneptus, a, um, adj.
2. in-aptus
,
unsuitable, impertinent, improper, tasteless, senseless, silly, pedantic, absurd, inept, without tact (class.): quem enim nos ineptum vocamus, is mihi videtur ab hoc nomen habere ductum, quod non sit aptus. Idque in sermonis nostri consuetudine perlate patet. Nam qui aut tempus quid postulet, non videt, aut plura loquitur, aut se ostentat, aut eorum quibuscum est, vel dignitatis, vel commodi rationem non habet, aut denique in aliquo genere aut inconcinnus aut multus est, is ineptus esse dicitur,: nihil insolens aut ineptum,: negotium,: causa,: lusibus advertere numen ineptis,: sententiae inepto inanique impetu,: ineptus et jactantior hic paulo est (i. q. nimis officiosus, negotiosus ardelio),: chartae,waste-paper,: lictor,foolish, impertinent,.—Comp.: quod est multo ineptius,.— Sup.: ineptissimae figurae,: ineptissimum est, with a subject - clause, ; .— As an abusive epithet: quid est, inepta, quid rides?; so, inepte,; ; .— Adv.: ĭneptē, improperly, impertinently, foolishly, absurdly, ineptly (class.): interdum inepte stultus es,: disserere,: dicere,: nil molitur inepte,: inepte et frigide uti verbis,: fautor ( = favens),: cornicari,. — Comp.: delirare,.— Sup.: ineptissime fieri,.

la:noun:inebriatio.html:
ĭnēbrĭātĭo, ōnis, f.
inebrio
,
inebriation (late Lat.), Aug. de Civ. Dei, 16, 1.

la:adj:inexercitatus.html:
ĭn-exercĭtātus, a, um, adj.
Untrained, unexercised, unpractised, unskilful (class.): rudis et inexercitatus miles,; so, miles,: homo non hebes, neque inexercitatus,: promptus et non inexercitatus ad dicendum,: histriones,: copiae,: eloquentia,.—
Unemployed, not busy (rare): homo, Cels. praef. fin.

la:adj:inexorabilis.html:
ĭn-exōrābĭlis, e, adj.
That cannot be moved by entreaty, inexorable (class.).
Of persons, constr. with in, adversus, contra, or dat.
With in and acc.: qui inexorabilis in ceteros esse visus sum,.—
With adversus: adversus te et rem tuam,.—
With contra: contra improbos nocentesque,.—
With dat.: delictis,.— (ε) Absol.: ni me inexorabilem faxis, Pac. ap. : judices,: Achilles,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: res,: disciplina,inexorably severe, rigorous,: odium,: fatum,: claustra,.— *
That cannot be obtained by entreaty: neque inexorabile certe, Quod petimus,.

la:adj:inevitabilis.html:
ĭn-ēvītābĭlis, e, adj.,
unavoidable, inevitable (post-Aug.): fulmen,: mala,: fatum,; cf.: sors fati,: crimen,.—Plur. subst.: ĭnēvītābĭlĭa, .—Adv.: ĭn-ēvītābĭlĭter, unavoidably, inevitably: nos compellit,.

la:adj:inexpugnabilis.html:
ĭn-expugnābĭlis, e, adj.,
that cannot be taken by assault, impregnable, inexpugnable (class.)
Lit.: arx,: urbes,

; .—

Trop., unconquerable, in assured safety: homo,: terra,impenetrable,: gramen,that cannot be rooted out,: pectus Amori,: finitio verborum,: necessitas dormiendi,.

la:noun:inedia.html:
ĭnĕdĭa, ae, f.
2. in-edo
,
an abstaining from food, fasting (class.): tenebrae oboriuntur, genua inediā succidunt,: vigiliis et inedia necatus,: inediam sustinere,: inediā vitam finire, i. e. to starve one's self to death, ; cf.: inediā mori,.— In plur.: inedias durare,.

la:adj:inexcusabilis.html:
ĭn-excūsābĭlis, e, adj.,
that cannot be excused, inexcusable (poet. and post-class.): ne te retrahas, et inexcusabilis absis,: tempus,: onera,that cannot be refused,: necessitas, Cod. Th. 11, 16, 7 al.—Comp., .

la:adj:inenarrabilis.html:
ĭn-ēnarrābĭlis, e, adj.,
that cannot be related or described, indescribable (mostly post-Aug.): mira quadam et incredibili atque inenarrabili pietate,: labor,: tabes (jecoris),: natura fluminum,: ratio,: habitus,.

la:adj:inefficax.html:
ĭn-effĭcax, ācis, adj.,
ineffectual, inefficient (post-Aug.).
With gen.: vox inefficax verborum,unproductive of, unable to produce,.—
Absol.: ratio,: dii,.— Comp., : parentes inefficacissimi, i. e. very weak, Inscr. ap. Grut. 415, 10.—Adv.: ĭneffĭcācĭter, ineffectually, in vain, ; ; .

la:adj:inelegans.html:
ĭn-ēlĕgans, antis, adj.,
not choice or elegant; tasteless, inelegant (class.): orationis non inelegans copia,: deliciae (with illepidae),: odor non inelegans,a not unpleasant odor,.—
Transf., unreasonable, inconsistent (late Lat.): nam inelegans esse visum est ex heredis persona incipere obligationem,.— Adv.: ĭnēlĕganter, not choicely, tastelessly, inelegantly: scribere,; : dividere,without discrimination, without judgment,; .

unexpected (class.).
Of persons: in armis Hostis adest,.—
